question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given in the table below. Find $\text{E}[Y{X}^{2}].$

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.2$ | $0$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.7$ | $0.1$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with supports ${S}_{X}$ and ${S}_{Y},$ respectively, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability mass function with support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}.$ If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=y{x}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y) \\  & =(2\cdot {1}^{2})\cdot f(1,2)+(4\cdot {1}^{2})\cdot f(1,4)+(2\cdot {2}^{2})\cdot f(2,2)+(4\cdot {2}^{2})\cdot f(2,4) \\  & =2\cdot f(1,2)+4\cdot f(1,4)+8\cdot f(2,2)+16\cdot f(2,4) \\  & =2\cdot 0.2+4\cdot 0+8\cdot 0.7+16\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0.4+0+5.6+1.6 \\  & =7.6.\end{aligned}
$$
